partners.mechanism_chain: CYP26C1 (HGNC:20036) —DISRUPTS→ Retinoic acid metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-70190); Retinoic acid metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-70190) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal skeletal development (HP:0000924); CYP27B1 (HGNC:2407) —PRODUCES→ 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D (CHEBI:17720); 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D (CHEBI:17720) —DISRUPTS→ Vitamin D metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-168799); Vitamin D metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-168799) —LEADS_TO→ Rickets (HP:0002757); Vitamin D metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-168799) —LEADS_TO→ Hypocalcemia (HP:0003153); Abnormal skeletal development (HP:0000924) —LEADS_TO→ Rickets (HP:0002757); Abnormal skeletal development (HP:0000924) —LEADS_TO→ Hypocalcemia (HP:0003153). Loss-of-function mutations in CYP26C1 disrupt retinoic acid metabolism, indirectly impacting downstream pathways that influence skeletal development. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in CYP27B1 directly impair the production of the active form of vitamin D (1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D), a critical metabolite for calcium absorption and bone mineralization. Both disruptions converge on abnormal skeletal development and rickets, with hypocalcemia as a shared consequence.

#### 1. vitamin D-dependent rickets, type 1A  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.573)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-211916)

**Proposed mechanism:** CYP26C1 (HGNC:20036) —DISRUPTS→ Retinoic acid metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-70190); Retinoic acid metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-70190) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal skeletal development (HP:0000924); CYP27B1 (HGNC:2407) —PRODUCES→ 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D (CHEBI:17720); 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D (CHEBI:17720) —DISRUPTS→ Vitamin D metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-168799); Vitamin D metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-168799) —LEADS_TO→ Rickets (HP:0002757); Vitamin D metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-168799) —LEADS_TO→ Hypocalcemia (HP:0003153); Abnormal skeletal development (HP:0000924) —LEADS_TO→ Rickets (HP:0002757); Abnormal skeletal development (HP:0000924) —LEADS_TO→ Hypocalcemia (HP:0003153). Loss-of-function mutations in CYP26C1 disrupt retinoic acid metabolism, indirectly impacting downstream pathways that influence skeletal development. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in CYP27B1 directly impair the production of the active form of vitamin D (1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D), a critical metabolite for calcium absorption and bone mineralization. Both disruptions converge on abnormal skeletal development and rickets, with hypocalcemia as a shared consequence.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of mutations in CYP26C1 in patients presenting with severe rickets and hypocalcemia, or the identification of a common genetic variant in CYP26C1 with a high allele frequency (>1%) in gnomAD that is statistically associated with Disease A, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this overlap could inform therapeutic strategies. For Disease A, interventions aimed at modulating vitamin D signaling might be beneficial, while for Disease B, therapies that bypass or supplement active vitamin D could be explored. Identifying shared downstream pathways could also lead to novel therapeutic targets for both conditions.

Loss-of-function mutations in CYP26C1 (involved in retinoic acid degradation) and ALDH1A2 (involved in retinoic acid synthesis) both impair the retinoic acid signaling pathway. This disruption leads to a spectrum of developmental defects, including limb abnormalities (Disease A) and cardiovascular defects and diaphragmatic hernia (Disease B).

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in CYP26C1 do not affect retinoic acid levels or downstream signaling, or that ALDH1A2 mutations do not impact retinoic acid synthesis, in relevant developmental contexts. _(variant: Absence of pathogenic variants in gnomAD for the identified causal variants in CYP26C1 and ALDH1A2.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of retinoic acid signaling in these distinct developmental disorders could reveal common therapeutic targets or strategies for intervention, potentially enabling the development of treatments that address multiple congenital anomalies stemming from this pathway.
